The Hornbostel–Sachs system of instrument classification lists this class under the heading "duct flutes, or flutes with a duct". The label "fipple flute" is often applied to members of that subgroup, but there is no general agreement on the structural details of the sounding mechanism that makes a fipple flute what it is.

歐洲導管笛類有久遠歷史：西約克郡馬爾姆荒原出土羊骨笛，1952年原定為鐵器時代，: European duct flutes have a long history: a sheep-bone pipe was found on Malham Moor in the West Riding of Yorkshire, dated in 1952 to the Iron Age and reassigned by recent research to a period after the Roman conquest; the museum on the Isle of Bute holds a flute confirmed as Iron Age. The Wicklow pipe from Ireland may be the oldest find, and a replica fitted with a duct can be played. MacCullough notes that the oldest surviving whistle belongs to the twelfth century, but early Irish law of the seventh and eighth centuries already mentions court pipers. The Tusculum whistle is a fourteenth- to fifteenth-century piece of copper or bronze, now in the National Museum of Scotland. Fourteenth-century recorders have been excavated from the moat at Dordrecht in the Netherlands and from a latrine at Göttingen in Germany, with further examples from Esslingen, Tartu, Rhodes and Elbląg in Poland.
豎笛具有清亮透徹的音色質感，帶有溫和的音響特徵。其音域寬闊，從低音區的深沉厚重到: The fipple flute has a clear, transparent timbre with a mild acoustic character. Its range is wide, with distinct layers running from the deep, heavy bass to the sharp, bright treble. It resonates in a distinctive way: the sound is produced mainly by the air column in the body, so the timbre keeps its warmth while still carrying lightly. Compared with the softness of woodwind instruments it is more spirited; compared with the heaviness of brass it seems slender and nimble. Its characteristic mouthpiece design (the fipple) gives the tone a slight rustling quality that adds a distinctive expressiveness. The fipple flute is used in both folk and classical music, and its timbre is highly malleable: it can be gentle and moving, or lively and leaping.
豎笛材質因年代與地域而異。古代標本多由羊骨製成，如鐵器時代出土的骨製豎笛。托斯庫: The materials of the fipple flute vary with period and region. Ancient specimens are mostly made of sheep bone, such as the bone flutes excavated from the Iron Age. The Tusculum whistle is made of copper or bronze. Instruments of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance usually had a body of a hardwood such as ash, maple or hazel, with a wooden or bone fipple duct at the mouthpiece, and the edges of the fingerholes were sometimes inlaid with bone or ivory for durability. Modern instruments are mostly made of selected woods or ABS resin.
